newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.N. opposes Panama's repatriation of Colombians.
newsitem.headline: U.N. opposes Panama's repatriation of Colombians.

text.p: The main United Nation refugee agency opposes Panama's decision to repatriate Colombian refugees to their homeland, a senior U.N. offical in Panama said on Monday.
"The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is against the repatriation because we can't confirm that they were repatriated voluntarily," regional deputy head Flor Rojas told Reuters.

Panamanian and Colombian officials reached an agreement over the weekend for repatriation of about 300 Colombians, mostly women and children, to Bahia Cupica, a tourist area on Colombia's Pacific coast, she said. They had fled several weeks ago from violence between guerrilla groups and right-wing death squads in Colombia's northwest region of Uraba along Panama's border.

"International accords establish criteria of voluntary repatriation with conditions of security and dignity. We cannot ensure these occurred," Rojas said, adding that the UNHCR was not invited to see all the sites where the refugees had sought shelter.
